rewrites.comment: The tracker is a hash-routed SPA, so every path under /app must serve its shell. This must come BEFORE the catch-all below.

headers.comment: Default everything to revalidate. cleanUrls means a page is served at '/', which an /index.html rule never matches — without this it inherits Firebase's 1h default and a phone keeps running the previous deploy. The hashed-asset rules below override this.
The tracker is private and must never be indexed. The public marketing pages at /, /privacy and /terms deliberately are, so this header is scoped to /app rather than applied site-wide.
Exercise animation frames are content-hash named, so they can be cached forever. Regenerating a clip changes its filename, so a stale copy is never served.
Marketing screenshots and the OG card are not content-hashed, so they get a day rather than a year — long enough to be free on repeat visits, short enough that replacing one is visible the next day.
